newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's government debt closed lower on Monday, pulled down by a negative trend in Bunds and U.S. Treasurys, ahead of Spanish Treasury auctions of new strippable debt on Tuesday and Wednesday, dealers said.

"It's mainly down because of foreign markets," a dealer with a big Spanish investment house said. But also the auctions, especially after the Treasury offered a total of 600 billion pesetas in the four maturities (three-, five-, 10- and 15-year bonds) were adding pressure, he said.
"We're underperforming Italian market due to the auctions," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, trader at ABN Amro in Madrid.

But traders added a good level of demand was likely to show up at tomorrow's auction of three- and 10-year bonds, as buying was boosted by the exemption of 25 percent witholding tax on these new issues.

"I expect demand will be around 200 billion pesetas each, with yields not far from the current market's levels. Let's say at 5.25 percent for the three-year and at 6.35 percent for the 10-year bond," the domestic dealer said.
"People are selling to make room for the bonds at tomorrow's auction," said Arechederra, adding that after Tuesday's results the market could show a quick recovery.

Chartists said the closing level above the support standing at 116.52 was a godd sign, and they added that the long bond future could easily break two resistances first at 116.96 and the second one at 117.10.
More in general, dealers said trading volume in Spanish government debt was low and the market lacked of fresh news, about the economic trend and the EMU outlook.
The 10-year spread over Bunds, trading at 66 basis points at the close, was seen to remain around those levels for few more months, dealers added.
